questions.text: A page must load the same visual rules across 20 HTML files. Which change best minimizes duplicated styling while keeping later updates consistent?
options: Put a style attribute on each element
Add one linked external stylesheet and reference it from each page
Repeat a style block in every page's head
Use the deprecated font tag throughout

questions.text: A user types a domain name, but the browser needs the destination IP address. Which service resolves that name before the connection is made?
options: HTTP
FTP
DNS
CSS

questions.text: A page contains an image that conveys information. Which implementation best preserves that information for a user who cannot see the image?
options: Use a descriptive alt value conveying the image's meaning
Set the image width and height explicitly
Put the filename in the title attribute only
Use CSS background-image with no accompanying text

questions.text: A form must allow exactly one answer from three mutually exclusive choices, while also allowing several independent preferences to be checked. Which pairing is appropriate?
options: Checkboxes for the single answer; radio buttons for preferences
Select elements for both, regardless of interaction
Radio buttons sharing a name for the single answer; checkboxes for preferences
Text inputs for both to preserve flexibility

questions.text: A table has a heading cell that should span three columns. A developer uses rowspan="3". What is the actual issue and correction?
options: rowspan is valid only on headings; replace it with scope
rowspan spans rows, so use colspan="3"
rowspan requires CSS grid; use display: table
No issue: rowspan and colspan are interchangeable

questions.text: A stylesheet rule `.notice { color: blue; }` should affect only the element whose id is `notice`. Which change most directly matches the requirement?
options: Change `.notice` to `#notice` and assign id="notice"
Keep `.notice` and assign class="notice"
Change color to background-color
Move the rule into an inline style without changing the selector

questions.text: A registration page needs (1) styles shared by all pages, (2) one page-specific layout rule, and (3) one urgent single-element override. Which strategy is most maintainable while satisfying all three?
options: Put every rule inline so precedence is predictable
Use a linked stylesheet for shared rules, an internal style block for page-specific rules, and inline styling only for the exceptional element
Use only an internal style block and copy it to each page
Use deprecated HTML presentation tags for shared rules and CSS for the rest

questions.text: A student says a form's `method="get"` is preferable because the form contains a password and GET is easier to debug. Which response best identifies the decisive security issue?
options: GET always encrypts values in transit, so it is preferable
GET prevents values from appearing in browser history
GET commonly places submitted values in the URL; use HTTPS and a suitable POST flow, while recognizing POST alone is not encryption
POST makes the form secure even over unencrypted HTTP

questions.text: An image is purely decorative, a nearby caption already gives the same information, and a screen reader is announcing the filename as duplicate content. Which is the best fix?
options: Remove the image so the layout is simpler
Use an empty alt attribute for the decorative image
Repeat the caption in alt text so both are available
Move the filename to the image title attribute

questions.text: A layout works on desktop but its fixed-width content overflows on a narrow phone. Which change best addresses the cause without discarding the layout rules?
options: Set a larger fixed width so the browser scales it
Replace every class selector with an id selector
Add a viewport meta tag only; fixed-width content will then always fit
Use responsive sizing and a media query at an appropriate viewport width, and ensure the viewport is configured
